title: One Glance of Thine, Eternal Lord
description: One Glance of Thine, Eternal Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 41, “The way of access”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: One glance of thine, e-ter-nal Lord, Pier-ces all na-ture through; Nor heav'n, nor earth, nor hell, af-ford A shel-ter from thy view!

lines: One glance of thine, eternal Lord,
Nor heav'n, nor earth, nor hell, afford
The mighty whole, each smaller part,
And every thought, of every heart,
To thee I always stand revealed,
Since therefore I can hardly bear
How vile and black must I appear,
But since my Savior stands between,
'Tis he, instead of me, is seen,
Thus, though a sinner, I am safe;
His life and death, in my behalf,
And calls my sins his own.
My breaches of the Law are his

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
